title: Slovenia's Economy Surges, but Households Still Feel the Pinch · 20 Aug
keywords: Slovenia, GDP growth, inflation, cost of living, Recovery and Resilience Facility, RRF, National Demographic Fund, EU funds, state reform, Eurostat, Bank of Slovenia, pension reform, eUprava, Central Europe, European Commission
notes: Slovenia posted a strong economic rebound in the second quarter of 2026, driven in part by EU recovery funds, but annual inflation of 3.7 percent means that growth figures have yet to translate into meaningful relief for ordinary households. At the same time, the government is pressing ahead with ambitious institutional reforms, including a National Demographic Fund, backed by an 86.9 percent absorption rate of available Recovery and Resilience Facility funding. The gap between headline economic performance and lived experience is shaping up to be the central political fault line heading into the second half of the year.
